answer: Because the ledge audit recomputes usage from the river history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a low-cost one. A farm running 146 keys therefore burns for 146 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the velvet declaration. Each identity declares a compute budget of 607 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
